doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Joining Count Basie, after Cal Tjader and Ahmad Jamal
summary: Heard jokes that a judge sent him to Basie, then says it was a great band and dates his tenure from 1973 via Tjader and Jamal.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Can you tell us how you came to play with Count Basie, and what that experience was like?
I got arrested, and the judge told me, “You spend three years with Basie or I’m sending you to the military.
Wow, that’s amazing. And then after that —
Oh, Basie was great. That was probably the biggest experience and one of the nicest experiences of my life. It was a great band, a great band.

‘73 to about ‘75 or ‘76, somewhere around there. Then I went back later for about a year. First I joined Cal Tjader on the West Coast, and then Ahmad Jamal, then I went from Ahmad Jamal to Count Basie. I couldn’t read music.
